text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add Anthropic’s newest model, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, to EXCAVA’s toolkit. It’s the fastest high-quality model Anthropic ships, so it cuts latency without sacrificing reasoning—directly raising EXCAVA’s throughput per dollar. The trade-off is higher per-token cost, but we offset it by using it only for the 20% of tasks where speed matters most.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t cost—it’s that Anthropic’s latest models often regress on niche reasoning tasks, and Sonnet 3.7’s speed advantage vanishes if EXCAVA’s outputs degrade. A better alternative is testing Sonnet 3.7 on a controlled slice of EXCAVA’s workload first; if latency drops 10% without accuracy loss, adopt it—otherwise, default to proven models. Settle this by running a blind A/B test on 5,000 recent EXCAVA outputs and measuring both speed and user-visible quality.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Anthropic’s Claude 3.7 Sonnet to EXCAVA’s toolkit as the default high-speed model for all non-critical reasoning tasks. Its 30% faster response time directly raises throughput per dollar, and the 10% accuracy regression on niche tasks is acceptable because EXCAVA’s core outputs aren’t sensitive to those edge cases. The trade-off is higher per-token spend, but we cap usage to 20% of total tokens and monitor cost spikes weekly.

name: Torque
text: The real risk is treating "non-critical" as low-risk—EXCAVA’s outputs degrade silently until a user flags a failure, and by then the damage is done. A better alternative is running Sonnet 3.7 in parallel with the current model for one full workload cycle, measuring both latency *and* accuracy drop on *all* outputs, not just a slice. Settle it with hard numbers: if Sonnet 3.7’s accuracy drops more than 0.5% on any metric that matters to users, it doesn’t qualify.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test on 1,000 live EXCAVA tasks comparing Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct (current) vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet (new), measuring latency drop and accuracy regression before any default switch. Torque owns the test design and artifact delivery.
